dedupe_keys.name: battery free medium wave am radio hoopra for disaster information kanto and fukui japan

description: This study revisits the role of medium-wave AM broadcasting in public safety on the centenary of the Great Kanto Earthquake and of radio broadcasting in Japan. The author's hoop-shaped radio (HOOPRA) is a battery-free receiver powered only by the radio waves; the paper determines its maximum reception distance for NHK stations JOFG (927 kHz, 5 kW) in Fukui and JOAK (594 kHz, 300 kW) and JOAB (693 kHz, 500 kW) in the Kanto region. It finds that about 38 million people in Kanto within an 80 km radius of JOAK or JOAB, and about 0.4 million people in Fukui within 15 km of JOFG, can receive broadcasts with HOOPRA, and that since most stations run 5 kW the radio is usable within 15 km of each. The paper argues for re-evaluating terrestrial medium-wave broadcasting as an emergency information source ahead of the predicted Nankai Trough earthquake. Producer: the HOOPRA author, published in the Journal of Disaster Research 18-6 (2023), eight pages with two figures. Coverage: two areas of Japan. Access: free preprint on arXiv. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: reception distances are computed for one receiver design and given stations, and do not model power outages of the transmitters. Simulation uses: it provides population within reception range for emergency broadcast coverage and resilience models. Related record: Australia's broadcasting resilience program (case_study-australia-broadcasting-resilience-program).
